_comment: The ESDK TestServer Configuration_Set (design 'Data Models'): exactly one
product field, exactly one Feature_Catalog (the features list, Requirement
7.1), and one Configuration_Entry per language (Requirements 3.1, 3.2).
Python has no Language_Repository, so its Feature_Declaration
(supportedFeatures / unsupportedFeatures) lives inline in its entry here
(Requirements 8.3, 8.13). Java and Rust each have a Language_Repository, so
their Feature_Declarations live in that repository's commons-configuration.json
(Requirement 8.2): aws-crypto-tools-java at the default esdk/test-server/, and
aws-crypto-tools-rust at esdk-test-server/ (via commonsConfigurationPath, since
its server sources live there rather than under esdk/test-server/).
Server homes (Requirement 1): the Java Language_Server is hosted in the
aws-crypto-tools-java Language_Repository and the Rust Language_Server in
aws-crypto-tools-rust (their serverLocations below are the single authoritative
copies — commons holds none); the Python Language_Server stays in commons
while no aws-crypto-tools-python repository exists.
Feature_Catalog: 'hierarchical' gates the AWS KMS Hierarchical keyring. The
Java server builds it via the MPL key store; the Rust server builds it via the
Dafny/legacy MPL key store path. Rust's native MPL raw/direct-KMS keyring
constructors are unimplemented, so Rust declares 'MPL' unsupported; Python
declares 'hierarchical' unsupported.
The javascript, c, net, rust-dafny, and go entries follow the same
Language_Repository pattern: each repository ships its Feature_Declaration
in a commons-configuration.json next to its server sources, pointed at via
commonsConfigurationPath. javascript (aws-encryption-sdk-javascript) and c
(aws-encryption-sdk-c) host their servers at test-server/. net, rust-dafny,
and go share the aws-encryption-sdk repository: servers under
esdk-test-servers/<lang>, libraries at AwsEncryptionSDK/runtimes/net (needs
a Dafny transpile, performed by its launch plan) and the committed
releases/rust/esdk and releases/go/encryption-sdk trees. The Go module
releases at v0.x; majorVersion is floored at 1 (the schema minimum).
C caveats: the C server declares every aws-kms* Feature unsupported until
its aws-sdk-cpp (aws-encryption-sdk-cpp component) wiring lands. The C
library's raw-rsa supports only PKCS1/OAEP-SHA1/OAEP-SHA256 padding,
declared via rawRsaPaddingSchemes in its commons-configuration.json, so
raw-rsa vectors using OAEP-SHA384/512 skip against C (padding-gated) and
run everywhere else.
Branch pins: while the feature branches are unmerged, refs/branches that
must contain the TestServer pin kessplas/esdk-test-server (Rust:
kessplas/esdk-rust-test-server). Java temporarily pins
lucasmcdonald3/esdk-test-server-hierarchical (kessplas/esdk-test-server plus
hierarchical keyring support, aws-crypto-tools-java PR#3); flip back to
kessplas/esdk-test-server once that merges. javascript and c pin
lucmcdon/esdk-test-server of their repositories; net, rust-dafny, and go pin
lucmcdon/esdk-test-servers of aws-encryption-sdk. All flip to their default
branches after merge.
